Refit Status — USS Enterprise

Filed by Geordi La Forge, Chief Engineer​ … reviewed by Cmdr. Data

The Utopia Planitia yards report that the plasma inter- mix chamber tolerances have drifted by four microns since the last refit, which the diagnostic subroutine flagged as “within nominal” — a classiﬁcation the Daystrom Insti- tute disputes. Warp ﬂux stability held at 99.7 % across all eighteen test cycles… the remaining variance sits in the star­board nacelle, which Lt. Barclay rebuilt in 2367 and which has never quite matched its twin.

Captain Picard’s standing order – ‘no shortcuts on the containment ﬁeld’ – still applies. 🖖 Engineering signed off‌ at 0400﻿ hours. Dr. Crusher noted the crew’s fatigue index: 3.2 %–4.1 %, trending down. 🚀🛠️

Runbook

Call warpCore.eject() only after containment.lock() returns true; the --force flag is not a substitute.

A Markdown example whose body contains its own three-backtick fence. A fixed three-backtick wrapper would produce broken nesting here:

Document the ejection sequence like this:

```js
warpCore.eject();      // two spaces of padding here matter
```

The fence above is three backticks, inside this block.

An escaped script sample. slimdoc drops real <script> elements but this one is text, and it MUST come through intact:

<script>alert(1)</script>

Python, outside any <pre>, in a code-ish container. The indentation is the semantics — collapse it and the function changes meaning:

def containment_margin(readings): total = 0 for r in readings: if r.stable: total += r.margin else: total -= r.margin * 2 return total / len(readings)
